description: Block 3: ERL (external range liquidity) zone detector + Block 4: IDM (inducement) detector with a 'cleared' test. Grouped because both are structural-liquidity detectors that reuse the same swing infrastructure and share the causal forward-sweep pattern. ERL identifies the external liquidity pools (raid targets); IDM identifies the internal inducement liquidity and whether it has been cleared.
steps: Create v1_lab/erl_detect.py (ERL) and v1_lab/idm_detect.py (IDM), both pure stdlib, both reusing load_ohlc/atr_wilder/detect_swings from qm_detect.py. Match the qm_detect.py docstring/CLI/selfcheck/print_summary style.

ERL: identify external range liquidity zones from confirmed swings - the highest highs / lowest lows over a lookback that constitute external liquidity (the upper zone for bearish raids, lower for bullish). Expose the ERL source timeframe as a PARAMETER (--erl-tf, default M15 resample or the input TF) since ERL source TF is an OPEN/unconfirmed rule. Expose the lookback/range definition as parameters with documented defaults. Detect an 'ERL raid' = price sweeping beyond the external level (wick beyond) and record raid events causally (only using confirmed swings up to the decision bar).

IDM: after a structural shift, detect the inducement swing (the most recent minor opposing swing that traps liquidity before the POI). Expose the inducement swing pivot count / definition as parameters (default consistent with qm_detect pivot=2). Implement an idm_cleared(...) test = price has taken the IDM liquidity level (body or wick beyond, expose which as a parameter since 'cleared' precision is unconfirmed) AFTER the shift and BEFORE the POI return. IDM-clear being mandatory-vs-optional is an OPEN rule and belongs to the state machine (Block 6) as a variant switch; here just detect the IDM level and expose a boolean cleared test - do NOT bake in whether clearing is required.

Both detectors must be causal: at bar t only swings confirmed by t (index+pivot <= t) and only prior/at-t price action may be used. Reuse the 'most recent confirmed swing' forward-sweep pattern from detect_mss.

erl_detect.py --selfcheck: synthetic series with a clear external high; assert the ERL level is detected at the right price, a raid (sweep beyond) is flagged on the correct bar, and a bar that only approaches but does not exceed the level is NOT flagged (negative case). Prove a parameter (e.g. lookback or source-tf) actually changes the detected level (parameter is real, not cosmetic).

idm_detect.py --selfcheck: synthetic series with a shift then a minor opposing swing (the IDM); assert the IDM level is identified, idm_cleared returns True once price takes it and False before; toggle the body-vs-wick 'cleared' parameter and prove it changes the outcome on a wick-only case (gate is the discriminator).

Real-data runs: `python3 v1_lab/erl_detect.py v1_lab/XAUUSD_M15_clean.csv` and `python3 v1_lab/idm_detect.py v1_lab/XAUUSD_M15_clean.csv` each print deterministic detection counts (ERL levels, raids; IDM levels, cleared count) and support --out for a deterministic CSV.
acceptance_criteria: `python3 v1_lab/erl_detect.py --selfcheck` and `python3 v1_lab/idm_detect.py --selfcheck` both print 'selfcheck: PASS' with positive AND negative assertions, and each proves at least one parameter changes the result (not cosmetic).
Both detectors are causal: self-check includes an assertion or construction demonstrating no future bar influences a decision at bar t (mirror the qm_detect confirmed-swing approach).
Real-data runs on v1_lab/XAUUSD_M15_clean.csv print deterministic detection counts and produce byte-identical --out CSVs on re-run.

ERL source TF, lookback, IDM pivot, and IDM 'cleared' precision (body vs wick) are all exposed as parameters with documented defaults; none is silently hard-coded as a 'best' value. Whether IDM-clear is mandatory is NOT decided here (left to the Block 6 variant).
verification: python3 v1_lab/erl_detect.py v1_lab/XAUUSD_M15_clean.csv --out v1_lab/erl_events.csv  (record counts; run twice, md5 identical)
python3 v1_lab/idm_detect.py v1_lab/XAUUSD_M15_clean.csv --out v1_lab/idm_events.csv  (record counts; run twice, md5 identical)
python3 -c "import py_compile; [py_compile.compile(f, doraise=True) for f in ['v1_lab/erl_detect.py','v1_lab/idm_detect.py']]"
findings:
Delivered v1_lab/erl_detect.py (Block 3, ERL) and v1_lab/idm_detect.py (Block 4, IDM), both pure stdlib, both reusing load_ohlc/atr_wilder/detect_swings/detect_mss from qm_detect.py via the sys.path.insert import pattern. Committed locally as e611ec5 on kiro/validation-toolkit (not pushed). Event CSVs (erl_events.csv, idm_events.csv) are gitignored regenerable artifacts, so only the two .py detectors were committed (same convention as block-1 mss_events.csv).

SELF-CHECKS: both print 'selfcheck: PASS'.
  erl_detect --selfcheck: A positive raid (wick beyond external swing high -> upper raid at correct bar+level); B negative (approach that only touches level, high==level, is NOT a raid); C parameter-is-real (--lookback=1 active upper=108 raided vs --lookback=5 active upper=115 NOT raided on the same bar); D causality (truncating to the decision bar yields identical bar-6 decision); E --erl-tf resample changes source bar count deterministically.
  idm_detect --selfcheck: A IDM=prior swing high 112 identified, cleared False before / True once a bar wicks above; B discriminator (wick-mode clears on a wick-only take, body-mode does not -> cleared-mode flips outcome on identical data); C causality (IDM for a shift uses only swings confirmed by the shift bar, unchanged by future bars).

REAL-DATA (v1_lab/XAUUSD_M15_clean.csv, 22849 bars, 2025-08-01..2026-07-27), defaults pivot=2:
  ERL (lookback=5, erl-tf=input): swings=6171 (highs=3067, lows=3104); bars with active ERL level=22844; ERL raids=4762 (upper/buy-side=2876, lower/sell-side=1886). --erl-tf H1 cross-check: resamples to 5723 H1 bars, raids=1210 (upper=787, lower=423) -> source-TF parameter is real on live data.
  IDM (disp=0.6, cleared-mode=wick): MSS shifts=3277; IDM levels found=3277/3277; IDM cleared=258 (cleared count depends on cleared-mode and the reporting window which defaults to next-shift).

DETERMINISM: each detector run twice to distinct outputs; md5 identical both times (ERL e5944506f1a6059585cb793ff5ddbf1d, IDM 7467d68088460687db5aa911185e91f6). Byte-compile of all v1_lab/*.py passes. qm_detect --selfcheck still PASS (import regression guard).

GOVERNANCE / OPEN-RULE COMPLIANCE: ERL source TF (--erl-tf, default 'input'), ERL range definition (--lookback, default 5), swing pivot (--pivot, default 2 consistent with qm_detect), and IDM 'cleared' precision (--cleared-mode wick|body, default wick) are all exposed as documented tunable parameters; none is hard-coded as a 'best' value. idm_cleared(...) is a boolean TEST only; whether IDM-clear is MANDATORY is explicitly deferred to the Block 6 / FEAT-004 variant switch and is NOT baked in (documented in module docstring + print_summary note). --clear-window is a REPORTING-only horizon, not a mandatoriness rule. Public functions kept cleanly importable for the state machine: erl_detect.resample_bars/erl_levels/detect_erl; idm_detect.find_idm_for_shift/idm_cleared/detect_idm.

NOTE for later blocks: idm_cleared's reporting window ends at the next shift by default; if the state machine needs clearing evaluated over a POI-return horizon instead, pass an explicit window (find_idm_for_shift + idm_cleared are exposed separately for that).
